html:
The We Wai Kum, or Campbell River First Nation, are one of the groups of the Laich-kwil-tach, the southernmost branch of the Kwakwaka'wakw, on the east coast of Vancouver Island in British Columbia.

The map shows them at Campbell River in 1492, but in that year the area was home to Salish-speaking peoples such as the K'ómoks. The Laich-kwil-tach moved south from the Johnstone Strait area during the 1800s and took over the Campbell River area.

Like other Kwakwaka'wakw, they lived from salmon and the sea in villages of cedar plank houses, and marked rank and family rights through the potlatch. Their close kin are the We Wai Kai of Quadra Island.
sum: The We Wai Kum, or Campbell River First Nation, are one of the groups of the Laich-kwil-tach, the southernmost branch of the Kwakwaka'wakw, on the east coast of Vancouver Island in British Columbia.
